transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-10
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Martin Lee (Redwood AE); Sana Patel (Redwood SE); Dr. Emily Santos (Coastal Clinic, CTO); Rajiv Kumar (Head of MLOps); Anna Bell (Legal)

Summary (auto):
Quick POC scoping to align on data handling requirements for a 4-week evaluation. Main topics: PII handling, logging & redaction, retention settings, storage of prompts and transcripts, and benchmarking plan for latency/cost. Ask: whether Redwood Hosted is acceptable or Dedicated/private required for PHI.

Topics:
- Success criteria and benchmarks
- Workload sizing and sample traffic
- PII redaction & logging controls
- Retention and prompt storage policies
- Next steps and legal docs

Transcript:
[00:00] Martin Lee: hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
[00:03] Dr. Emily Santos: yes, hi martin, thanks. we have maybe 45 minutes, we wanted to focus on data handling specifics because obviously we're HIPAA territory.
[00:12] Martin: totally, totally. quick intro, i'm martin lee, AE at Redwood, with sana our solutions eng, she'll run the tech bits. can i hand it to sana?
[00:19] Sana Patel: hi all, hi emily, rajiv, anna. quick agenda: success criteria, traffic profile, then deep-dive on PII/retention, then benchmark plan. sound good?
[00:28] Dr. Emily Santos: yep. we have three success criteria: 1) latency under 300ms 95th for short clinical queries, 2) no PHI leaves our VPC or is stored unencrypted, and 3) reproducible outputs for triage classification.
[00:41] Rajiv Kumar: and cost target, we want to see per-1k token cost so leadership can eval.
[00:45] Sana: great, that helps. quick clarifying q: are you planning to use hosted API or dedicated/private deployment for the POC?
[00:52] Dr. Emily Santos: ideally hosted to start, but legal might push Dedicated or Private if prompt storage is an issue. anna, any initial thoughts?
[01:00] Anna Bell: yep, if prompts include PHI we need either customer-managed keys or private deployment. we also need audit logs and DPA addenda.
[01:09] Martin: understood. high level on options: Hosted = fastest to spin up, we can support configurable retention windows and scrubbers; Dedicated = reserved capacity + optional VPC peering and customer KMS; Private = full control on-prem or in your VPC.
[01:22] Rajiv: can you explain how logging works in Hosted? like are prompts stored in plaintext, and for how long?
[01:27] Sana: by default we keep logs for 30 days for debugging, but for POCs we can set retention to 0 or disable persistent transcript storage. we also have an ingest-level redactor that can mask common PHI patterns (SSNs, MRNs, phone numbers). warning: pattern redaction is heuristic and can miss edge cases.
[01:44] Dr. Emily Santos: and where are the logs stored? region wise?
[01:47] Martin: stored encrypted at rest in our cloud region — you can pick region, and for Dedicated we can configure customer KMS so keys are managed by you.
[01:56] Anna Bell: do you do deterministic hashing for identifiers so we can join events without storing raw PII?
[02:01] Sana: yes, we support salted hashing at ingest; salt can be customer-provided when using customer-managed keys. note though that for some downstream model tuning we usually need unhashed prompts, so that's a tradeoff.
[02:13] Rajiv: hmm ok. what about prompt storage for debugging or evals — we want to avoid storing full prompts. can you store only embeddings or hashes?
[02:20] Martin: we can store embeddings instead of raw prompt text in some flows; embeddings are not reversible in practice, however for paper-trail debugging you may want text. for POC we recommend embedding-only storage plus sample redacted transcripts saved off-line.
[02:34] Dr. Emily Santos: what about function calls or structured outputs — any chance sensitive fields get written to logs?
[02:39] Sana: function outputs can be configured to be scrubbed. we can apply per-route post-processing rules to drop or redact specific JSON fields before persistence. this is part of our Redwood Console routing rules, though i might have said 'Redwood Consol' earlier on other calls — sorry, force of habit.
[02:55] Rajiv: how about KV cache? we are worried that cached prefixes might include PHI.
[02:59] Sana: good q — our KV cache is ephemeral in memory for Dedicated/private, and for Hosted we use a sharded in-memory cache; cache persistence beyond request is optional and disabled for PHI-sensitive routes. we sometimes call it 'KV cash' in notes, transcript errors noted.
[03:15] Martin: let's talk retention windows — typical options we've used with healthcare customers: 0 days (no storage), 7 days (debugging short), 30 days (standard POC), 90 days (longer eval). we can also sign off bespoke retention in the DPA.
[03:28] Anna Bell: 0 days or 7 days preferred for initial validation. we need to see how debugging will work if nothing is stored.
[03:34] Sana: for debugging with 0-day retention we do ephemeral capture during a session and then expire; also we can set up a secure, customer-owned S3 with lifecycle policies where redacted logs are pushed — that gives you auditability without Redwood retaining raw prompts.
[03:49] Dr. Emily Santos: what about redaction accuracy? we can't rely on heuristics for PHI.
[03:53] Sana: agreed — redaction is an assist, not a guarantee. recommended approach: client-side masking of obvious PHI before send + server-side scrubbers + policy to reject requests that fail schema checks. we can provide sample middleware for your ingestion pipeline.
[04:09] Rajiv: benchmarking: we want to run a 1k request/day workload or roughly 100 RPS spikes, with 50 token avg per request. does that map to your earlier docs?
[04:18] Martin: yep, that's helpful. for sizing we'll simulate a 100 RPS burst with average sequence length 50 tokens, plus kv cache warmup. we'll share a benchmark harness that you can run against Hosted and Dedicated endpoints.
[04:28] Sana: timeline wise: share harness + sample schema by Dec 14; you provide anonymized 1k records by Dec 13; we run benchmarks week of Dec 20; share results and tune config by Dec 27.
[04:39] Dr. Emily Santos: good. on encryption in transit & at rest, we need TLS + AES-256 and ability to audit key rotations.
[04:45] Martin: we support TLS everywhere and AES-256 at rest. for Dedicated with customer KMS we can log key usage to your audit stream; we can also support HSM-backed keys for enterprise.
[04:55] Anna Bell: DPA question: does Redwood sign Business Associate Agreement (BAA) for HIPAA?
[04:59] Martin: we have an enterprise compliance track and can execute a BAA for Dedicated/Private customers — we'll send template. for Hosted small POCs we typically ask that PHI be minimized unless Dedicated is procured.
[05:11] Rajiv: what about prompt retention for model tuning? we will not allow Redwood to use our data for model training.
[05:16] Sana: we have an explicit data use setting: "no training" for your org — that prevents model updates with your data and is enforceable via config + contract. we'll include that in paperwork.
[05:27] Dr. Emily Santos: nice. a nit: how do you handle system prompts and prompt templates? are those stored alongside user text?
[05:33] Sana: system templates are stored as part of route config; they can be marked as ephemeral and not persisted. we can also serve templates from your config store so Redwood never stores them.
[05:42] Martin: another question for you emily/rajiv: do you need PII-preserving analytics, like counts by cohort but no raw text?
[05:48] Rajiv: yes, aggregated metrics are fine — we want token/latency/cost metrics, and error rates.
[05:53] Sana: Redwood Console will give per-route token and cost breakdowns; audit logs can be redacted and routed to your S3.
[05:58] Anna Bell: about legal, we need to review logs access controls — RBAC and SSO.
[06:02] Martin: we support SAML SSO, role-based access control with audit trails, and can integrate with your IdP.
[06:09] Dr. Emily Santos: one more on telemetry — do you collect prompts in traces?
[06:13] Sana: traces can contain spans with shortened prompts, but trace collection for PII routes can be disabled; we recommend masking at the agent. note: sometimes our auto-transcribe labels mix name entities, e.g., 'Redwood Dediacated' in older notes.
[06:27] Rajiv: ok what about POC success criteria formalization? we need acceptance: 95th latency < 300ms, token cost less than $X (we'll confirm), and no retained raw PHI.
[06:38] Martin: we'll map those to test cases in the benchmark. also we'll produce a runbook for redaction and incident response.
[06:45] Dr. Emily Santos: can you confirm that when retention is set to 0, no transcripts are stored and logs are ephemeral? we want written confirmation.
[06:52] Martin: yes we'll provide a retention matrix in writing and include it in the DPA addendum.
[06:57] Anna Bell: for the DPA, can you also put SLAs around data deletion timing?
[07:01] Martin: yes, we can specify deletion windows and provide verification logs of deletion.
[07:06] Sana: technical note: for Hosted, even with 0 retention we may keep short-lived debug artifacts in ephemeral storage for up to 5 minutes for request correlation; we'll document that and propose alternatives (customer-owned S3 or Dedicated).
[07:18] Rajiv: are there any limitations in your model infra around encrypted payloads? like can we send encrypted blobs that the model shouldn't see?
[07:25] Sana: if it's encrypted end-to-end, the model can't process it — so if you want the model to operate you need plaintext or client-side masking. we do support envelope encryption for transit to storage though.
[07:36] Dr. Emily Santos: ok. can you outline the benchmark steps again?
[07:39] Sana: step 1: run baseline run against Hosted with sample data and retention 30 days; step 2: run with retention 0 and client-side redaction to measure perf delta; step 3: run on Dedicated with customer KMS and warm cache. we'll provide scripts.
[07:52] Martin: we'll include perf metrics (P50/P95/P99), token cost, and memory/kv cache behavior.
[07:58] Rajiv: any known issues with sequence length and kernel perf? we saw in past notes that long contexts spike latency.
[08:03] Sana: yes long context (>1024 tokens) increases latencies non-linearly. we recommend prompt engineering to trim context and use KV caching for repeated prefixes. we'll also show quantization options for Dedicated.
[08:16] Dr. Emily Santos: final question: storage of prompts for short-term troubleshooting — can that be restricted to a named engineer with audit trail rather than org-wide?
[08:23] Martin: yes RBAC lets you restrict access to specific engineers and every access is logged.
[08:28] Anna Bell: that works.
[08:30] Martin: ok next steps recap: i'll send SOC2 & KMS docs, sana will share the benchmark harness and sample schema, rajiv provide anonymized sample records, anna confirm DPA timeline. we'll schedule the benchmark week of Dec 20.
[08:43] Dr. Emily Santos: thanks, this was useful.
[08:45] Martin: thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email with artifacts.
